day: # Reading the Word of God: a three-year plan of daily Bible readings, prepared by
# Lutheran Church–Canada, the Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod and the North American
# Lutheran Church (2018), from its calendars for 2018, 2019 and 2020:
#   10 June 2021, "Three-year schedule of daily Bible readings for 2021 to 2023"); the 2021
#   2018 festival readings and the 2018 sequence, ending on 31 December with Psalm 150 and Acts 15:1–21.
# Each day has an Old Testament reading, a psalm and a New Testament reading, read in
# order through the year; fourteen festivals have readings of their own instead, and the
# sequence waits for them (2018: Genesis 4 on 5 January, Genesis 5 on 7 January).
#   plan:N   the Nth day of the calendar year that is not one of the plan's festivals.
#   The festival rows are keyed by their date rules (01-06, easter-49 = the Transfiguration
#   on the last Sunday after the Epiphany, easter-46, easter-7, easter-3, easter-2, easter,
#   easter+39, easter+49, 10-31, 11-01, start = the First Sunday in Advent, 12-24, 12-25);
#   those keys are the days the sequence skips.
#   cycle    the plan's year: 2018 (Genesis to Judges 9; Matthew to Acts 15), 2019 (Judges 10
#   to Isaiah 25; Acts 15 to John 1), 2020 (Isaiah 26 to Malachi; John 1 to Revelation).
#   A calendar year Y reads the cycle C with (Y - C) divisible by 3: 2021, 2024 ... read 2018's.
# A common year has 351 plan days and a leap year 352.  The 2018 and 2019 sequences have
#   351 sets and 2020's (a leap year) 352: in a leap year of the 2018 or 2019 cycle the last
#   plan day has none, and in a common year of the 2020 cycle the 352nd set is read with the
#   351st on the last plan day (31 December).  The calendars published so far (2018-2023)
#   include neither case, so this is inferred, not printed.
# The festivals keep their printed headings (2021: Christmas Eve, Christmas Day).  Citations are given as printed, with the book names spelled out and en dashes; the
#   psalms of the festivals (e.g. Psalm 72, Psalm 110:1–4) are as printed.  Slips of the
#   print are corrected and listed in docs/source-errors.csv.
